newsitem.title: FRANCE: Unions call for stoppages at Renault plants.
newsitem.headline: Unions call for stoppages at Renault plants.

text.p: Trade unions called on workers to stage one-hour work stoppages at Renault car plants on Thursday as the company presented a plan to cut 2,764 jobs in France this year to its French staff council.
Some 500 Belgian workers from the Vilvoorde plant slated for closure were heading for the nearby French plant of Douai, which assembles the new Megane models, to join in the protests.

The secretary of the French staff council said he would propose to seek expert comment on the company's proposed job cuts. Council sources said that if his motion was approved, it could have the effect of delaying the plan by several weeks.

Earlier a senior politician in France's ruling coalition said Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer had committed an "irreparable mistake" in the way he announced the closure of the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium and should quit.

Jean-Francois Mancel, secretary-general and number two to Prime Minister Alain Juppe in the conservative Gaullist RPR party, told Europe 1 radio that Schweitzer had "committed a very serious mistake by offending human dignity".

The chairman of the recently-privatised car firm, expected to announce heavy losses next week, triggered political anger in Belgium and France by announcing on February 27 the closure of the plant in the Brussels suburbs, with the loss of 3,100 direct jobs.

Renault announced a week later that it planned to accelerate its job reduction programme in France, eliminating 2,764 posts this year, up from 1,640 in 1996, but Schweitzer said he did not expect outright layoffs.
